story.title: Why the Cowboys and Lions always play on Thanksgiving Day: All 32 NFL team's record on the holiday
story.summary: A look at the records and traditions in the NFL on Thanksgiving Since the beginning of time — okay, maybe not that long ago, but since very early in National Football League history, fans have been able to watch the Dallas Cowboys and Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving Day . This year, the Lions will kick off the holiday, hosting the Chicago Bears at Ford Field. The Cowboys will host the Philadelphia Eagles , and the Thanksgiving action will conclude with the Buffalo Bills hosting the Kansas City Chiefs. Bears vs. Lions will be played at 1 p.m. ET on CBS and stream on Paramount+ , Eagles vs. Cowboys will take place at 4:30 p.m. ET on FOX, and the Chiefs and Bills will battle it out in a game that could determine the No. 1 seed in the AFC at 8:20 p.m. on NBC. The Lions started their tradition in 1934, when owner George A. Richards set out to attract more fans. The marketing wizard's plan…
